Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

2	
3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	读完本讲，你应该能够：
6	
7	1. 用一句话说清 **Muon 是什么**：一个专门为神经网络**隐藏层权重矩阵**设计的优化器，其余参数（embedding、输出头、增益/偏置）仍然用 AdamW 训练。
8	2. 说出 Muon 的来源与战绩：它诞生于 Keller Jordan 的 NanoGPT / CIFAR-10 训练速度竞赛（speedrun），后来被 Kimi.ai 等机构用于大规模语言模型训练。
9	3. 记住一句话级的算法摘要：**先跑普通 SGD 动量，再把更新用 Newton-Schulz 迭代正交化**。
10	4. 看懂 README 中的标准用法代码：`use_muon=True/False` 参数组 + `MuonWithAuxAdam`。

13	## 2. 前置知识
14	
15	本讲是整套手册的第一篇，不假设你读过任何深度学习框架源码。只需要理解下面几个概念（都用大白话解释）：
16	
17	| 术语 | 通俗解释 |
18	|---|---|
19	| 参数 / 权重矩阵 | 神经网络里可学习的数据。隐藏层的参数通常是二维矩阵（形状如 512×256），本讲的主角就是它们。 |
20	| 优化器（optimizer） | 决定「拿到梯度之后，参数往哪个方向、走多远」的算法，例如 SGD、Adam、AdamW。 |
21	| 梯度下降与学习率（lr） | 梯度指出下坡方向，学习率决定每步走多远。 |
22	| 动量（momentum） | 把历史梯度做指数加权平均再走，像小球带惯性，能冲过噪声和震荡。 |
23	| 权重衰减（weight decay） | 每步把参数略微乘小一点（如 ×0.999），防止参数无限变大。AdamW 就是 Adam + 解耦权重衰减。 |
24	| 正交矩阵 | 满足 \( Q^\top Q = I \) 的方阵。直觉上：它只做「旋转/反射」，**不拉伸任何方向**，所有列向量的长度都是 1。 |
25	| 谱范数（spectral norm） | 一个矩阵对向量最多能拉伸多少倍，等于最大奇异值。本讲只需这个直觉，第 2 单元再展开。 |
26	| 奇异值分解（SVD） | 任何矩阵都能写成 \( G = U S V^\top \)，其中 \( S \) 是对角矩阵，对角线上的数叫奇异值，描述 \( G \) 在各方向上的拉伸强度。 |
27	| embedding / head / gains / biases | 输入查表矩阵 / 网络最后一层（输出头）/ 隐藏层的缩放系数和偏置。这些**不是**标准二维权重，README 建议它们继续用 AdamW。 |
28	| speedrun | 「用最少算力/时间把模型训到某个精度」的竞赛，例如 2.6 A100 秒训 CIFAR-10 到 94% 准确率。 |
29	| bfloat16 | 一种 16 位浮点数，指数位与 float32 相同、精度更低，GPU 上算得快、数值范围还不容易溢出。 |
30	
31	如果你对「正交矩阵」「SVD」还不熟也不必担心——本讲只需要「把更新的各方向拉伸强度拉平」这个直觉，数学细节在第 2 单元专门讲。

63

182	### 4.2 muon.py 顶部两个函数：正交化与更新计算
183	
184	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
185	
186	这两个函数是 Muon 的「算法心脏」，所有优化器类都只是围绕它们的壳。
187	
188	**为什么需要正交化？** 一个普通梯度矩阵 \( G = USV^\top \) 在不同方向上的拉伸强度（奇异值）参差不齐：有的方向更新量很大、有的很小。把更新替换成**最接近的正交矩阵** \( UV^\top \)（相当于把所有奇异值统统拉平为 1），能让更新在各个方向上能量均衡，且更新大小只由学习率决定——这就是 docstring 中「lr 以谱范数为单位」的由来。
189	
190	**为什么要用 Newton-Schulz 迭代而不是直接算 SVD？** 直接 SVD 又慢又难以在低精度下跑。Newton-Schulz 迭代**只用矩阵乘法**就能逼近「矩阵的零次幂」\( G(G^\top G)^{-1/2} \approx UV^\top \)，而且数值上足够稳定，可以在 GPU 上用 bfloat16 跑——又快又省显存。
191	
192	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
193	
194	`zeropower_via_newtonschulz5(G, steps)` 的伪代码：
195	
196	```text
197	输入：矩阵 G，迭代步数 steps
198	X ← G 转成 bfloat16
199	若 X 行数 > 列数：先转置（保证行 ≤ 列）
200	X ← X / ‖X‖          # 谱范数归一化，保证最大奇异值 ≤ 1
201	重复 steps 次：
202	    A ← X · Xᵀ
203	    B ← b·A + c·A²    # 组合成五次多项式
204	    X ← a·X + B·X     # 朝正交矩阵推进一步
205	若转置过：转置回原形状
206	返回 X                # 近似 U·S'·Vᵀ，S' 的对角元 ≈ 0.5 ~ 1.5
207	```
208	
209	数学目标（第 2 单元详细推导）：
210	
211	\[
212	\text{zeropower}(G) \;=\; G\,(G^{\top}G)^{-1/2} \;=\; U V^{\top}
213	\]
214	
215	`muon_update(grad, momentum, ...)` 把动量和正交化串成一次完整更新：
216	
217	```text
218	momentum ← β·momentum + (1-β)·grad          # 动量缓冲区（指数滑动平均）
219	update   ← (1-β)·grad + β·momentum           # Nesterov 形式（可关）
220	若 update 是 4 维（卷积核）：压成 2 维矩阵
221	update   ← zeropower_via_newtonschulz5(update, ns_steps)
222	update   ← update × √max(1, 行数/列数)        # 与形状相关的尺度缩放
223	返回 update
224	```
225	
226	#### 4.2.3 源码精读
227	
228	**① `zeropower_via_newtonschulz5` 的 docstring——最重要的免责声明**：[muon.py:L5-L14](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L5-L14)
229	
230	```python
231	def zeropower_via_newtonschulz5(G, steps: int):
232	    """
233	    Newton-Schulz iteration to compute the zeroth power / orthogonalization of G. ...
234	    This iteration therefore does not produce UV^T but rather something like US'V^T
235	    where S' is diagonal with S_{ii}' ~ Uniform(0.5, 1.5), which turns out not to hurt model
236	    performance at all relative to UV^T, where USV^T = G is the SVD.
237	    """
238	```
239	
240	这段 docstring 诚实地说：**该迭代并不输出精确的 \( UV^\top \)**，而是输出 \( US'V^\top \)，其中 \( S' \) 的对角元近似均匀分布在 0.5～1.5——即「大致拉平、但不完全拉平」的奇异值。作者的经验是这**完全不伤**模型效果。系数选择是为了「最大化零点处斜率」以减少迭代步数，甚至宁可牺牲精确收敛。这是理解整个实现的钥匙。
241	
242	**② 迭代主体**：[muon.py:L16-L27](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L16-L27)
243	
244	```python
245	    a, b, c = (3.4445, -4.7750,  2.0315)
246	    X = G.bfloat16()
247	    if G.size(-2) > G.size(-1):
248	        X = X.mT
249	
250	    # Ensure spectral norm is at most 1
251	    X = X / (X.norm(dim=(-2, -1), keepdim=True) + 1e-7)
252	    # Perform the NS iterations
253	    for _ in range(steps):
254	        A = X @ X.mT
255	        B = b * A + c * A @ A # quintic computation strategy ...
256	        X = a * X + B @ X
257	```
258	
259	要点：
260	
261	- 三个系数 \( (a,b,c) \) 定义了一个**五次多项式迭代**（quintic）：\( X \leftarrow aX + (bA + cA^2)X \)，其中 \( A = XX^\top \)。
262	- 第 17 行 `G.bfloat16()`：整个迭代在 bfloat16 下进行，快且稳。
263	- 第 18-19 行：若行数多于列数则先转置，让矩阵变成「扁」的（行 ≤ 列），减少矩阵乘法的计算量，最后在 [muon.py:L29-L31](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L29-L31) 转置回去，保证输出形状和输入一致。
264	- 第 22 行：用 Frobenius 范数归一化保证谱范数不超过 1（Frobenius 范数 ≥ 谱范数，所以除以它一定把最大奇异值压到 1 以下），这是 Newton-Schulz 迭代收敛的必要条件。
265	
266	**③ `muon_update`：一次完整 Muon 更新**：[muon.py:L34-L41](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L34-L41)
267	
268	```python
269	def muon_update(grad, momentum, beta=0.95, ns_steps=5, nesterov=True):
270	    momentum.lerp_(grad, 1 - beta)
271	    update = grad.lerp_(momentum, beta) if nesterov else momentum
272	    if update.ndim == 4: # for the case of conv filters
273	        update = update.view(len(update), -1)
274	    update = zeropower_via_newtonschulz5(update, steps=ns_steps)
275	    update *= max(1, update.size(-2) / update.size(-1))**0.5
276	    return update
277	```
278	
279	逐行解读：
280	
281	- 第 35 行 `momentum.lerp_(grad, 1 - beta)`：`lerp_` 是线性插值原地操作，等价于 `momentum = beta*momentum + (1-beta)*grad`，即动量的指数滑动平均。
282	- 第 36 行：Nesterov 动量的紧凑两行写法——先用「新梯度」修正动量，再以 `beta` 权重混合回梯度本身；`nesterov=False` 时直接用动量缓冲区。
283	- 第 37-38 行：卷积核是 4 维张量（如 64×3×7×7），`view(len(update), -1)` 把它压成 64×147 的二维矩阵，之后就能走和普通权重完全一样的正交化流程。
284	- 第 40 行：尺度缩放因子 \( \sqrt{\max(1, m/n)} \)（\( m \) 为行数、\( n \) 为列数），配合正交化让**不同形状参数的更新 RMS 大体一致**，学习率因此获得「谱范数单位」的语义。推导在第 2 单元第 3 讲。

323	
324	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
325	
326	如果说前两个函数是「算法」，`Muon` 类的 docstring 就是「产品说明书」——它回答了三个设计问题：
327	
328	1. **Muon 这个名字**是 `MomentUm Orthogonalized by Newton-schulz`（动量 + Newton-Schulz 正交化）的缩写，一句话就是算法本身。
329	2. **架构定位**：Muon 不是从零发明的更新规则，而是「标准 SGD 动量 + 正交化后处理」的组合——先按你熟悉的动量法算出更新，再统一做正交化替换。
330	3. **超参语义**：学习率的单位是「每次更新的谱范数」，这和 AdamW 的「每个元素的幅度」完全不同量纲，是迁移使用时最容易踩的坑。
331	
332	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
333	
334	`Muon` 优化器每一步（`step()`）对每个参数做的事：
335	
336	```text
337	取参数 p 的梯度 p.grad
338	    ↓
339	惰性初始化动量缓冲区 momentum_buffer（首次为全零）
340	    ↓
341	update ← muon_update(p.grad, momentum_buffer, beta=momentum)   # 4.2 节的函数
342	    ↓
343	p ← p × (1 − lr × weight_decay)      # AdamW 式解耦权重衰减
344	p ← p − lr × update                  # 沿正交化后的更新走一步
345	```
346	
347	（分布式版 `Muon` 在此之上还有参数分片与 `all_gather` 同步，是全项目最难的部分，留到第 3 单元第 3 讲。）

# 第 1 讲 · 项目总览：Muon 是什么、为什么值得学

## 1. 本讲目标

读完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 用一句话说清 **Muon 是什么**：一个专门为神经网络**隐藏层权重矩阵**设计的优化器，其余参数（embedding、输出头、增益/偏置）仍然用 AdamW 训练。
2. 说出 Muon 的来源与战绩：它诞生于 Keller Jordan 的 NanoGPT / CIFAR-10 训练速度竞赛（speedrun），后来被 Kimi.ai 等机构用于大规模语言模型训练。
3. 记住一句话级的算法摘要：**先跑普通 SGD 动量，再把更新用 Newton-Schulz 迭代正交化**。
4. 看懂 README 中的标准用法代码：`use_muon=True/False` 参数组 + `MuonWithAuxAdam`。
5. 亲手跑通第一个脚本：实例化 `SingleDeviceMuonWithAuxAdam`，观察每个参数组被自动填充的默认超参。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲是整套手册的第一篇，不假设你读过任何深度学习框架源码。只需要理解下面几个概念（都用大白话解释）：

| 术语 | 通俗解释 |
|---|---|
| 参数 / 权重矩阵 | 神经网络里可学习的数据。隐藏层的参数通常是二维矩阵（形状如 512×256），本讲的主角就是它们。 |
| 优化器（optimizer） | 决定「拿到梯度之后，参数往哪个方向、走多远」的算法，例如 SGD、Adam、AdamW。 |
| 梯度下降与学习率（lr） | 梯度指出下坡方向，学习率决定每步走多远。 |
| 动量（momentum） | 把历史梯度做指数加权平均再走，像小球带惯性，能冲过噪声和震荡。 |
| 权重衰减（weight decay） | 每步把参数略微乘小一点（如 ×0.999），防止参数无限变大。AdamW 就是 Adam + 解耦权重衰减。 |
| 正交矩阵 | 满足 \( Q^\top Q = I \) 的方阵。直觉上：它只做「旋转/反射」，**不拉伸任何方向**，所有列向量的长度都是 1。 |
| 谱范数（spectral norm） | 一个矩阵对向量最多能拉伸多少倍，等于最大奇异值。本讲只需这个直觉，第 2 单元再展开。 |
| 奇异值分解（SVD） | 任何矩阵都能写成 \( G = U S V^\top \)，其中 \( S \) 是对角矩阵，对角线上的数叫奇异值，描述 \( G \) 在各方向上的拉伸强度。 |
| embedding / head / gains / biases | 输入查表矩阵 / 网络最后一层（输出头）/ 隐藏层的缩放系数和偏置。这些**不是**标准二维权重，README 建议它们继续用 AdamW。 |
| speedrun | 「用最少算力/时间把模型训到某个精度」的竞赛，例如 2.6 A100 秒训 CIFAR-10 到 94% 准确率。 |
| bfloat16 | 一种 16 位浮点数，指数位与 float32 相同、精度更低，GPU 上算得快、数值范围还不容易溢出。 |

如果你对「正交矩阵」「SVD」还不熟也不必担心——本讲只需要「把更新的各方向拉伸强度拉平」这个直觉，数学细节在第 2 单元专门讲。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

Muon 是一个**极小而精**的研究型项目，整个仓库核心代码只有一个文件：

| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲是否涉及 |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | 项目定位、安装方式、标准用法、调参建议、战绩与延伸阅读 | ✅ 重点阅读 |
| `muon.py` | **全部核心实现**（约 290 行）：3 个函数 + 4 个优化器类 | ✅ 读顶部两个函数和 Muon 类 docstring |
| `setup.py` | 把单文件 `muon.py` 打包发布为 `muon-optimizer` 包 | 下一讲（u1-l2）精读 |
| `LICENSE` | MIT 许可证 | 不涉及 |

`muon.py` 内部结构一览（本讲先建立地图，后续各讲逐段精读）：

| 位置 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| [muon.py:L5-L31](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L5-L31) | `zeropower_via_newtonschulz5`：Newton-Schulz 迭代正交化（本讲 4.2） |
| [muon.py:L34-L41](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L34-L41) | `muon_update`：动量 + 正交化 + 缩放，组合成一次 Muon 更新（本讲 4.2） |
| [muon.py:L44-L96](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L44-L96) | `Muon`：分布式版优化器类，含核心 docstring（本讲 4.3） |
| [muon.py:L99-L127](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L99-L127) | `SingleDeviceMuon`：单机版，最适合入门阅读 |
| [muon.py:L130-L135](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L130-L135) | `adam_update`：30 行手写 AdamW 更新 |
| [muon.py:L138-L225](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L138-L225) | `MuonWithAuxAdam`：一个优化器同时跑 Muon + AdamW（分布式版） |
| [muon.py:L228-L287](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L228-L287) | `SingleDeviceMuonWithAuxAdam`：上述类的单机版，本讲综合实践的主角 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 README.md：项目定位、标准用法与战绩

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

README 开宗明义地回答了「Muon 是什么」：

> **Muon 是一个为神经网络隐藏层（hidden layers）权重设计的优化器。**
> 其他参数——例如 embedding、分类头、隐藏层的增益（gains）和偏置（biases）——应当继续使用标准 AdamW 优化。

这句话定义了 Muon 的**适用边界**：它不是「万能替换 AdamW」，而是**只接管隐藏层二维权重矩阵**，剩下的参数交给普通 AdamW。这一点贯穿整个项目的设计（第 3 单元会看到 `MuonWithAuxAdam` 就是为了「一个优化器管两类参数」而生）。

再用一句话概括 Muon 的算法（来自 `Muon` 类 docstring，4.3 节精读）：

> **Muon 内部先跑标准 SGD 动量，然后做一步「正交化后处理」：把每个二维参数的更新替换成最接近的正交矩阵。**

**它为什么值得学？** 三个理由：

1. **战绩硬**：把 CIFAR-10 训到 94% 的纪录从 3.3 A100 秒压到 2.6 A100 秒；把 GPT-2 (XL) 水平的训练成本压到 175 美元；被 Kimi.ai 用于前沿大模型训练。
2. **代码极小**：核心实现只有一个约 290 行的 `muon.py`，非常适合逐行精读、彻底吃透一个现代优化器。
3. **思想可迁移**：「动量 + 正交化后处理」和「以谱范数为单位的学习率」是理解一批新优化器（Shampoo、SOAP 等）的钥匙。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

README 的行文顺序就是一份使用说明书，阅读路线如下：

```text
标题：定位（hidden layers 专用优化器）
  └─ Installation：pip 直接从 GitHub 安装
      └─ Usage：标准用法代码（use_muon 参数组 + MuonWithAuxAdam）
          └─ Hyperparameter tuning：哪些超参要调、哪些不用调
              └─ Benchmarks / Accomplishments：对比实验与战绩
                  └─ More learning resources：延伸阅读
```

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**① 项目定位与出处**：[README.md:L1-L3](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/README.md#L1-L3)

```markdown
# Muon: An optimizer for the hidden layers of neural networks

This repo contains an implementation of the `Muon` optimizer originally described in [this thread] ...
```

标题点明定位；正文说明本仓库是 Keller Jordan 在 X（推特）上的帖子和文章中所述算法的参考实现。

**② 安装方式**：[README.md:L5-L9](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/README.md#L5-L9)

```text
pip install git+https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon
```

直接从 GitHub 仓库安装，不需要先手动下载。（打包细节在下一讲剖析 `setup.py`。）

**③ 标准用法：把一个 AdamW 训练脚本改造成 Muon**：[README.md:L13-L33](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/README.md#L13-L33)

```python
# optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=3e-4, betas=(0.90, 0.95), weight_decay=0.01)

# To replace the above, do the following:

from muon import MuonWithAuxAdam
hidden_weights = [p for p in model.body.parameters() if p.ndim >= 2]
hidden_gains_biases = [p for p in model.body.parameters() if p.ndim < 2]
nonhidden_params = [*model.head.parameters(), *model.embed.parameters()]
param_groups = [
    dict(params=hidden_weights, use_muon=True,
         lr=0.02, weight_decay=0.01),
    dict(params=hidden_gains_biases+nonhidden_params, use_muon=False,
         lr=3e-4, betas=(0.9, 0.95), weight_decay=0.01),
]
optimizer = MuonWithAuxAdam(param_groups)
```

这段代码是全项目最重要的使用范式，逐行拆解：

- 注释掉的一行是「改造前」：所有参数一个 AdamW 搞定。
- 改造的关键是**把参数分成两组**，塞进一个优化器：
  - `p.ndim >= 2` 的隐藏层权重 → `use_muon=True` 组，用 Muon 训练（注意 Muon 组**没有** `betas`，因为动量只有一个系数 `momentum=0.95`）；
  - 一维的增益/偏置（`ndim < 2`）、输出头、embedding → `use_muon=False` 组，用内部 AdamW 训练，超参和原来 AdamW 一致。
- `MuonWithAuxAdam(param_groups)` 之后，训练循环里只需要 `optimizer.step()` 一个调用，不再需要分别 step 两个优化器。

**④ 适用范围的补充说明**：[README.md:L35-L36](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/README.md#L35-L36)

README 提醒：示例中的 `model.body` / `model.head` / `model.embed` 要换成你自己模型里对应的模块；对卷积网络，**除第一层外的所有卷积核**都可以用 Muon 训练，其余用 AdamW。

**⑤ 调参建议**：[README.md:L44-L47](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/README.md#L44-L47)

> 默认的 momentum（0.95）、nesterov（True）、ns_steps（5）通常就够了，**只有学习率和权重衰减需要调**。学习率内置 muP 缩放：模型变大时无需重新调 lr。

### 4.2 muon.py 顶部两个函数：正交化与更新计算

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

这两个函数是 Muon 的「算法心脏」，所有优化器类都只是围绕它们的壳。

**为什么需要正交化？** 一个普通梯度矩阵 \( G = USV^\top \) 在不同方向上的拉伸强度（奇异值）参差不齐：有的方向更新量很大、有的很小。把更新替换成**最接近的正交矩阵** \( UV^\top \)（相当于把所有奇异值统统拉平为 1），能让更新在各个方向上能量均衡，且更新大小只由学习率决定——这就是 docstring 中「lr 以谱范数为单位」的由来。

**为什么要用 Newton-Schulz 迭代而不是直接算 SVD？** 直接 SVD 又慢又难以在低精度下跑。Newton-Schulz 迭代**只用矩阵乘法**就能逼近「矩阵的零次幂」\( G(G^\top G)^{-1/2} \approx UV^\top \)，而且数值上足够稳定，可以在 GPU 上用 bfloat16 跑——又快又省显存。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

`zeropower_via_newtonschulz5(G, steps)` 的伪代码：

```text
输入：矩阵 G，迭代步数 steps
X ← G 转成 bfloat16
若 X 行数 > 列数：先转置（保证行 ≤ 列）
X ← X / ‖X‖          # 谱范数归一化，保证最大奇异值 ≤ 1
重复 steps 次：
    A ← X · Xᵀ
    B ← b·A + c·A²    # 组合成五次多项式
    X ← a·X + B·X     # 朝正交矩阵推进一步
若转置过：转置回原形状
返回 X                # 近似 U·S'·Vᵀ，S' 的对角元 ≈ 0.5 ~ 1.5
```

数学目标（第 2 单元详细推导）：

\[
\text{zeropower}(G) \;=\; G\,(G^{\top}G)^{-1/2} \;=\; U V^{\top}
\]

`muon_update(grad, momentum, ...)` 把动量和正交化串成一次完整更新：

```text
momentum ← β·momentum + (1-β)·grad          # 动量缓冲区（指数滑动平均）
update   ← (1-β)·grad + β·momentum           # Nesterov 形式（可关）
若 update 是 4 维（卷积核）：压成 2 维矩阵
update   ← zeropower_via_newtonschulz5(update, ns_steps)
update   ← update × √max(1, 行数/列数)        # 与形状相关的尺度缩放
返回 update
```

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**① `zeropower_via_newtonschulz5` 的 docstring——最重要的免责声明**：[muon.py:L5-L14](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L5-L14)

```python
def zeropower_via_newtonschulz5(G, steps: int):
    """
    Newton-Schulz iteration to compute the zeroth power / orthogonalization of G. ...
    This iteration therefore does not produce UV^T but rather something like US'V^T
    where S' is diagonal with S_{ii}' ~ Uniform(0.5, 1.5), which turns out not to hurt model
    performance at all relative to UV^T, where USV^T = G is the SVD.
    """
```

这段 docstring 诚实地说：**该迭代并不输出精确的 \( UV^\top \)**，而是输出 \( US'V^\top \)，其中 \( S' \) 的对角元近似均匀分布在 0.5～1.5——即「大致拉平、但不完全拉平」的奇异值。作者的经验是这**完全不伤**模型效果。系数选择是为了「最大化零点处斜率」以减少迭代步数，甚至宁可牺牲精确收敛。这是理解整个实现的钥匙。

**② 迭代主体**：[muon.py:L16-L27](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L16-L27)

```python
    a, b, c = (3.4445, -4.7750,  2.0315)
    X = G.bfloat16()
    if G.size(-2) > G.size(-1):
        X = X.mT

    # Ensure spectral norm is at most 1
    X = X / (X.norm(dim=(-2, -1), keepdim=True) + 1e-7)
    # Perform the NS iterations
    for _ in range(steps):
        A = X @ X.mT
        B = b * A + c * A @ A # quintic computation strategy ...
        X = a * X + B @ X
```

要点：

- 三个系数 \( (a,b,c) \) 定义了一个**五次多项式迭代**（quintic）：\( X \leftarrow aX + (bA + cA^2)X \)，其中 \( A = XX^\top \)。
- 第 17 行 `G.bfloat16()`：整个迭代在 bfloat16 下进行，快且稳。
- 第 18-19 行：若行数多于列数则先转置，让矩阵变成「扁」的（行 ≤ 列），减少矩阵乘法的计算量，最后在 [muon.py:L29-L31](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L29-L31) 转置回去，保证输出形状和输入一致。
- 第 22 行：用 Frobenius 范数归一化保证谱范数不超过 1（Frobenius 范数 ≥ 谱范数，所以除以它一定把最大奇异值压到 1 以下），这是 Newton-Schulz 迭代收敛的必要条件。

**③ `muon_update`：一次完整 Muon 更新**：[muon.py:L34-L41](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L34-L41)

```python
def muon_update(grad, momentum, beta=0.95, ns_steps=5, nesterov=True):
    momentum.lerp_(grad, 1 - beta)
    update = grad.lerp_(momentum, beta) if nesterov else momentum
    if update.ndim == 4: # for the case of conv filters
        update = update.view(len(update), -1)
    update = zeropower_via_newtonschulz5(update, steps=ns_steps)
    update *= max(1, update.size(-2) / update.size(-1))**0.5
    return update
```

逐行解读：

- 第 35 行 `momentum.lerp_(grad, 1 - beta)`：`lerp_` 是线性插值原地操作，等价于 `momentum = beta*momentum + (1-beta)*grad`，即动量的指数滑动平均。
- 第 36 行：Nesterov 动量的紧凑两行写法——先用「新梯度」修正动量，再以 `beta` 权重混合回梯度本身；`nesterov=False` 时直接用动量缓冲区。
- 第 37-38 行：卷积核是 4 维张量（如 64×3×7×7），`view(len(update), -1)` 把它压成 64×147 的二维矩阵，之后就能走和普通权重完全一样的正交化流程。
- 第 40 行：尺度缩放因子 \( \sqrt{\max(1, m/n)} \)（\( m \) 为行数、\( n \) 为列数），配合正交化让**不同形状参数的更新 RMS 大体一致**，学习率因此获得「谱范数单位」的语义。推导在第 2 单元第 3 讲。

### 4.3 Muon 类 docstring：设计意图、适用边界与超参语义

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

如果说前两个函数是「算法」，`Muon` 类的 docstring 就是「产品说明书」——它回答了三个设计问题：

1. **Muon 这个名字**是 `MomentUm Orthogonalized by Newton-schulz`（动量 + Newton-Schulz 正交化）的缩写，一句话就是算法本身。
2. **架构定位**：Muon 不是从零发明的更新规则，而是「标准 SGD 动量 + 正交化后处理」的组合——先按你熟悉的动量法算出更新，再统一做正交化替换。
3. **超参语义**：学习率的单位是「每次更新的谱范数」，这和 AdamW 的「每个元素的幅度」完全不同量纲，是迁移使用时最容易踩的坑。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

`Muon` 优化器每一步（`step()`）对每个参数做的事：

```text
取参数 p 的梯度 p.grad
    ↓
惰性初始化动量缓冲区 momentum_buffer（首次为全零）
    ↓
update ← muon_update(p.grad, momentum_buffer, beta=momentum)   # 4.2 节的函数
    ↓
p ← p × (1 − lr × weight_decay)      # AdamW 式解耦权重衰减
p ← p − lr × update                  # 沿正交化后的更新走一步
```

（分布式版 `Muon` 在此之上还有参数分片与 `all_gather` 同步，是全项目最难的部分，留到第 3 单元第 3 讲。）

**① 名字与算法摘要**：[muon.py:L45-L53](https://github.com/KellerJordan/Muon/blob/f98f1cacc0263b04290753e32be8d498c1efc806/muon.py#L45-L53)

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
